title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week

    . This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Positive

Large-cap indices are now testing their declining 50-day moving averages, a key level that often acts as intermediate-term resistance. In the short term, price action has continued to firm up, with the 10- and 20-day moving averages curling upward as price consolidates above them. Mid- and small-cap indices are also showing improvement, though they have not yet reached their respective 50-day MAs.

On the sector front, leadership remains largely defensive. Consumer Staples, Utilities, and Communication Services continue to set the tone, while growth-oriented sectors such as Technology and Consumer Discretionary are staging modest bounces but remain in structurally weak, lagging positions.

Internally, market breadth and momentum metrics continue to improve. New highs are outpacing new lows, and upside momentum is expanding across market caps. This suggests steady demand pushing the average stock to new short-term highs, supported by broader participation—a constructive signal as the market navigates key resistance zones.

Plan of Action

Risk Management and Exposure Control

Maintain a Constructive but Disciplined Approach:
The market is building strength above rising 10- and 20-day moving averages, signaling short-term improvement. However, with major indices still testing the declining 50-day moving averages and defensive sectors leading, maintain a cautious bias while selectively leaning into strength.

Prioritize High-Quality, Technically Sound Setups:
Focus only on stocks showing relative strength, base breakouts, or early-stage trend reversals supported by volume. Avoid names with weak technical structure or those rallying off news without confirmation.

Scale Exposure Gradually:
Initial positions should remain modest. Add only as trades prove themselves and as broader market evidence — including participation and sector rotation — strengthens.

Actively Manage Existing Positions:
Exit or reduce exposure in trades that break down or fail to hold key breakout levels. Reallocate to stronger opportunities to maintain a higher-quality portfolio.

Market Monitoring and Internal Indicators

Watch the 50-Day Moving Average Closely:
The 50-day MA is a critical test of intermediate-term trend. A reclaim and hold would significantly improve the market’s technical tone. A rejection or stall here could lead to another pullback.

Track Internal Health for Continuation Signs:

  • Breadth and momentum should continue to expand.

  • New highs should sustain dominance over new lows.

  • Breakouts need to gain follow-through, not fade after one or two days.

Confirm Progress with Sector Rotation:
Look for sustained improvement in Technology, Consumer Discretionary, and Financials. Rotation into these areas would signal improving risk appetite and institutional interest.

Sector and Theme Development

Leadership Still Defensive — Watch for Transition:
While Consumer Defensive, Utilities, and Communication Services remain in leadership positions, they indicate a defensive bias. Watch for early signs of rotation into growth sectors for confirmation of a healthier rally.

Monitor Setup Expansion:
An expanding number of stocks building higher lows or breaking trendlines would suggest a growing opportunity set. This is crucial for a sustainable uptrend.

Capital Allocation and Trade Execution

Maintain a Moderate Cash Position:
Flexibility remains critical. Avoid being fully invested until indices reclaim and hold the 50-day MA and sector leadership broadens.

Implement Tight, Technical Stop-Losses:
Preserve capital by using well-defined exits. Risk/reward should be favorable before initiating any position.

Avoid FOMO and Chasing Strength:
Be disciplined. If you missed a move, wait for a secondary entry (pullback, base breakout). Avoid buying stretched setups or news-driven pops without structure.

Daily Reassessment and Adaptive Strategy

Review Key Metrics and Price Behavior Daily:

  • Are breakouts holding and expanding?

  • Are risk-on sectors gaining ground?

  • Is leadership clustering in healthier sectors?

Adjust Exposure Responsively:

  • If progress continues (breadth improves, 50-day reclaimed): scale in with confidence, but selectively.

  • If market stalls or breaks down at resistance: reduce exposure and reassess.

Let Setup Quality Be Your Guide:
Even with indices improving, only increase exposure if setups across individual stocks are expanding and showing follow-through.

Key Focus Areas

  • Patience and Confirmation: Don’t rush to deploy capital until the evidence supports a more durable trend.

  • Adaptability: Conditions can change quickly—stay nimble and open to both bullish and defensive pivots.

  • Emerging Themes and Relative Strength: Watch for clusters of strength in specific sectors, which may signal the next phase of market leadership.

Bottom Line

The market is showing encouraging early-stage strength, with indices climbing above short-term averages and internals improving. However, full confirmation will come only if the 50-day MAs are reclaimed and leadership rotates toward risk-on sectors. Stay cautiously constructive, focus on quality, and maintain a disciplined, flexible posture while the broader trend attempts to reassert itself.
